title: Mexican Government Plans Investment of 1.168 Trillion Pesos in Electricity and Gas Pipelines
author: Fernanda Monroy
content:
_This article by[Fernanda
Monroy](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/fermonroy/) originally appeared in
the [October 7, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/gobierno-preve-
inversion-de-un-billon-168-mil-millones-de-pesos-en-electricidad-y-
gasoductos-2/), an investigative Mexican news outlet._

The federal government plans an investment of **1.168 trillion pesos** in
generation, transmission, distribution and gas infrastructure projects to
**expand and modernize the National Electric System** , reported the
**Secretary of Energy, Luz Elena González Escobar**.

During President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo's morning press conference, the
official detailed that **794 billion pesos** correspond to generation
projects; **161 billion** , to transmission, and **72.47 billion** , to
distribution.

Most of the resources, she explained, will be concentrated on the construction
and commissioning of infrastructure to produce electricity, including
renewable energy projects and combined cycle plants.

In transmission, the resources will go to expanding and modernizing the
networks that carry electricity from generating plants to consumption centers.
Meanwhile, the investment in distribution contemplates the expansion and
modernization of the networks that bring supply to homes, businesses and
industries, in addition to electrification works.

Explaining the origin of the resources for generation, Claudia Sheinbaum noted
that it contemplates financing from the Federal Electricity Commission
(**CFE**), as well as mixed and private projects.

The investment also includes **140 billion pesos for gas pipeline
infrastructure** , of which 53 billion will be invested by the CFE and 87
billion by the National Natural Gas Control Center (**Cenagas**).

The Secretary explained that this infrastructure is necessary because the
electricity sector consumes around **60 percent of the country 's natural
gas**, so expanding the network will make it possible to guarantee the supply
required for the generating plants.

Among the CFE projects are the **Cuxtal** gas pipeline, which will carry gas
from Tabasco to the Yucatán Peninsula; **Centauro del Norte** , which
comprises two sections between Baja California and Sonora, and the rerouting
of the **Guaymas-El Oro** gas pipeline, in Sonora.

On the part of Cenagas, the **Coatzacoalcos II** and **Naco-Hermosillo-
Guaymas** projects are under construction. In addition, construction of the
**Reynosa** bypass has been completed and it is about to enter operation.

In turn, the director general of the CFE, **Emilia Esther Calleja Alor** ,
reported that the expansion also contemplates **60 transmission projects** ,
with which the national power grid will reach nearly **115,000 kilometers**.

As part of the distribution and electrification works, Calleja Alor reported
that between 2025 and 2026 **more than 21,000 works** were carried out,
benefiting more than **600,000 people**.

The Secretariat of Energy detailed that the investment also contemplates
projects to expand electricity coverage and reduce gaps in access to the
service. It added that currently **99.88 percent of households** have
electricity and that the goal is to reach 99.9 percent before the end of the
administration.
